findings.title: Team permission check uses AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, which requires the user to be both admin and owner simultaneously. Since these are typically mutually exclusive role checks, team admins (and likely owners too) are denied, contradicting the variable name and intent. Should be `||`. Additionally `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` queries membership for team id 0 for personal bookings, which is a meaningless query.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` plus `new EventManager({...user, credentials})` builds the EventManager from the logged-in caller. But the handler also allows attendees and team admins/owners to add guests, in which case the calendar/video integration update is attempted with credentials of someone who does not own the booking's calendar entry, so `updateCalendarAttendees` will fail or silently not update the real event. The organizer (`booking.user`) credentials should be used instead.

findings.title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking
findings.body: Permission is granted if the caller's email appears among booking attendees (`isAttendee`). Combined with the broken team check, this means any invited guest can add unlimited external email addresses to someone else's booking, triggering emails/ICS updates and leaking booking details (title, description, meeting URL/password) to arbitrary addresses. Consider restricting to organizer/team admins, or gating on event type settings.

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but the incoming `guest` string is not normalized before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. A blacklisted address submitted with any uppercase characters (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com`) bypasses the filter. Lowercase the guest email before comparison (and ideally before persisting/dedup against existing attendees, which is also case-sensitive today).

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives unfiltered guest list and errors are swallowed
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input rather than `uniqueGuests`; guests that were filtered out (already attendees or blacklisted) are then classified as "new" in email-manager and receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification. Also the catch block logs only a static string via `console.log`, discarding `err`, making email failures undiagnosable.

findings.title: No booking status/time validation before adding guests
findings.body: The handler adds attendees to any booking found by id, including CANCELLED/REJECTED/PENDING bookings and past bookings. This sends confirmation emails and ICS REQUEST invites for events that are cancelled or already over. Validate `booking.status === ACCEPTED` (and probably that the booking is upcoming) before mutating.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event type disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other send* helper in this file checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` and accepts an `eventTypeMetadata` parameter. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and unconditionally emails organizer, team members and all attendees, breaking the documented ability to disable standard emails for an event type.

findings.title: MultiEmail imports from its own package barrel, creating a circular import
findings.body: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports this module (`./form/MultiEmailLazy`). This self-referencing cycle can yield undefined components at runtime depending on module evaluation order/bundler. Import the components from their relative paths (e.g. `../components/button`) as the sibling form components do.

findings.title: Initial empty email row makes the Add button always fail validation on first click
findings.body: `multiEmailValue` defaults to `[""]`, so if the user presses "Add" without typing, `z.string().email()` fails on the empty string and the generic "Emails must be unique and valid" error is shown rather than the field being treated as empty. Also the `multiEmailValue.length === 0` guard never triggers for this default. Filter out blank entries before validating/submitting.

findings.title: Add-guests action is offered for bookings where it cannot work
findings.body: The new `add_members` entry is added unconditionally to `editBookingActions`, which is also rendered for past bookings (`isBookingInPast && isConfirmed`) and for pending bookings. Users can open the dialog and submit for bookings where adding guests is meaningless or will fail server-side. Gate the action on upcoming/confirmed (and non-seated) bookings.
